5.1.definition: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance: the media access method prescribed by 802.11, which proactively avoids collisions instead of detecting them.
5.1.cloze: 802.11 prescribes ___ instead of collision detection, because a wireless client cannot hear while it is sending.
aliases: carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance
5.1.ru: Метод доступа к среде в 802.11: коллизии предотвращаются, а не обнаруживаются.

5.1.definition: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection: the media access method used by 802.3 wired Ethernet LANs.
aliases: carrier sense multiple access with collision detection
5.1.ru: Метод доступа проводного Ethernet 802.3: коллизия обнаруживается постфактум.

5.1.definition: The IEEE working group and standard that defined Ethernet for wireless LANs (WLANs).
5.1.ru: Стандарт IEEE для беспроводных LAN.

5.1.definition: The IEEE working group and standard that defined Ethernet for wired LANs.
5.1.ru: Стандарт IEEE для проводного Ethernet.

5.1.term: Why WLANs raise more privacy issues
5.1.definition: Radio frequencies can reach outside the facility, so the signal is available beyond the physical walls.
5.1.cloze: WLANs raise more privacy issues because ___ can reach outside the facility.
5.1.ru: Радиосигнал выходит за пределы здания.

5.1.definition: The 802.11 frame field that identifies the type of wireless frame and contains subfields for protocol version, frame type, address type, power management, and security settings.
5.1.ru: Поле кадра: тип кадра, версия протокола, управление питанием, настройки безопасности.

5.1.definition: The 802.11 frame field typically used to indicate the remaining duration needed to receive the next frame transmission.
5.1.ru: Сколько ещё времени нужно на приём следующего кадра.

5.1.definition: The 802.11 frame field that usually contains the MAC address of the receiving wireless device or AP.
5.1.ru: MAC получателя.

5.1.definition: The 802.11 frame field that usually contains the MAC address of the transmitting wireless device or AP.
5.1.ru: MAC отправителя.

5.1.definition: The 802.11 frame field that is usually missing, because it is used only in ad hoc mode.
5.1.cloze: ___ is usually missing from an 802.11 frame because it is used only in ad hoc mode.
5.1.ru: Обычно отсутствует, нужно только в ad hoc.

5.1.definition: Frame Check Sequence: the field used for Layer 2 error control in all Layer 2 frames.
5.1.ru: Контроль ошибок на канальном уровне.

5.1.definition: Ready to send: the message a wireless client sends to the AP to request dedicated access to the network.
5.1.ru: Запрос клиента на выделенный доступ к среде.

5.1.definition: Clear to send: the message a wireless client receives from the AP granting access to send.
5.1.ru: Разрешение от точки доступа на передачу.

5.1.term: Why a wireless client cannot detect a collision
5.1.definition: WLANs are half-duplex shared media, so a wireless client cannot hear while it is sending.
5.1.cloze: A wireless client cannot detect a collision because it cannot ___ while it is sending.
5.1.ru: Полудуплекс: во время передачи клиент не слышит среду.

5.1.term: What happens when no CTS is received
5.1.definition: The wireless client waits a random amount of time before restarting the process.
5.1.ru: Клиент ждёт случайное время и начинает заново.

5.1.term: The three stages of the 802.11 association process
5.1.definition: Discover a wireless AP, authenticate with the AP, associate with the AP.
5.1.ru: Обнаружить, аутентифицироваться, ассоциироваться.

5.1.definition: The network name that appears in the list of available wireless networks on a client; in organizations using multiple VLANs, each SSID is mapped to one VLAN.
5.1.ru: Имя беспроводной сети. В больших сетях один SSID на один VLAN.

5.1.definition: The association parameter that refers to the 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ad WLAN standards; devices in Mixed mode support clients connecting via multiple standards simultaneously.
5.1.ru: Какие стандарты 802.11 поддерживаются. Mixed mode держит сразу несколько.

5.1.definition: The association parameter that refers to the frequency bands used to transmit wireless data; it can be selected automatically or set manually when another device interferes.
5.1.ru: Частотные каналы, выбираются автоматически или вручную при помехах.

5.1.definition: Discovery mode in which the AP openly advertises its service by periodically sending broadcast beacon frames containing the SSID, supported standards, and security settings.
5.1.ru: Точка доступа сама рассылает beacon-кадры.

5.1.definition: Discovery mode in which the wireless client must know the SSID name and initiates the process by broadcasting a probe request frame on multiple channels.
5.1.ru: Клиент сам рассылает probe request. Нужен, если beacon отключён.

5.1.definition: The broadcast frame an AP sends periodically so wireless clients can learn which networks and APs are available in a given area.
5.1.ru: Широковещательный кадр-маяк точки доступа.

5.1.definition: The frame a wireless client broadcasts on multiple channels in active mode, including the SSID name and the standards supported.
5.1.ru: Запрос клиента в активном режиме.

5.1.term: How an AP with SSID broadcast disabled answers a probe request without an SSID name
5.1.definition: It does not respond at all; only APs configured to broadcast beacon frames answer with a probe response providing the SSID name.
5.1.ru: Точка со скрытым SSID на запрос без имени не отвечает.

5.1.definition: Wireless LAN Controller: the device into which all control and management functions of the APs on a network are centralized.
5.1.ru: Контроллер, куда вынесено управление всеми точками доступа.

5.1.definition: Lightweight AP: an AP that no longer acts autonomously and only forwards data between the wireless LAN and the WLC.
5.1.ru: Облегчённая точка доступа: только пересылает данные на контроллер.

5.1.term: The major benefit of centralizing AP management in a WLC
5.1.definition: Simplified configuration and monitoring of numerous access points.
5.1.ru: Проще настраивать и мониторить много точек сразу.

5.2.term: The four threats wireless networks are specifically susceptible to
5.2.definition: Interception of data, wireless intruders, denial of service (DoS) attacks, and rogue APs.
5.2.ru: Перехват данных, чужие клиенты, DoS, чужие точки доступа.

5.2.term: How interception of data is countered
5.2.definition: Wireless data should be encrypted to prevent it from being read by eavesdroppers.
Unauthorized users attempting to access network resources can be deterred through effective authentication techniques.

5.2.term: The three sources of wireless DoS attacks
5.2.definition: Improperly configured devices, a malicious user intentionally interfering with the wireless communication, and accidental interference.
items: A malicious user intentionally interfering with the wireless communication
5.2.ru: Кривая настройка, намеренные помехи, случайные помехи.

5.2.term: Which band is more prone to interference
5.2.definition: The 2.4 GHz band is more prone to interference than the 5 GHz band, so 5 GHz should be used in areas prone to interference.
5.2.cloze: The ___ GHz band is more prone to interference from microwave ovens, cordless phones and baby monitors.
5.2.ru: 2,4 ГГц шумнее, чем 5 ГГц: микроволновки, радиотелефоны, радионяни.

5.2.term: How to minimize DoS risk from misconfiguration and malicious attacks
5.2.definition: Harden all devices, keep passwords secure, create backups, and ensure that all configuration changes are incorporated off-hours.
5.2.ru: Харденинг, пароли, бэкапы, изменения конфигурации в нерабочее время.

5.2.definition: An AP or wireless router that has been connected to a corporate network without explicit authorization and against corporate policy.
5.2.cloze: A ___ is an AP connected to a corporate network without explicit authorization and against corporate policy.
5.2.ru: Точка доступа, подключённая в корпоративную сеть без разрешения.

5.2.term: What an attacker can do once a rogue AP is connected
5.2.definition: Capture MAC addresses, capture data packets, gain access to network resources, or launch a man-in-the-middle attack.
decoys: Rewrite the routing table of the ISP
5.2.ru: Собирать MAC-адреса и пакеты, лезть в ресурсы сети, устроить MITM.

5.2.term: A personal network hotspot as a rogue AP
5.2.definition: A user with secure network access enables their authorized Windows host to become a Wi-Fi AP, circumventing security measures so other unauthorized devices can access network resources as a shared device.
5.2.ru: Раздача Wi-Fi с рабочего ноутбука это тоже rogue AP.

5.2.term: How organizations prevent the installation of rogue APs
5.2.definition: Configure WLCs with rogue AP policies and use monitoring software to actively monitor the radio spectrum for unauthorized APs.
5.2.ru: Политики rogue AP на контроллере плюс мониторинг радиоэфира.

5.2.definition: An attack in which the hacker is positioned in between two legitimate entities in order to read or modify the data that passes between the two parties.
5.2.ru: Атакующий встаёт между двумя легитимными сторонами и читает или меняет трафик.

5.2.definition: A popular wireless MITM attack where an attacker introduces a rogue AP and configures it with the same SSID as a legitimate AP.
5.2.cloze: In the ___ attack, an attacker introduces a rogue AP configured with the same SSID as a legitimate AP.
5.2.ru: Поддельная точка с тем же SSID, что у настоящей.

5.2.term: Why airports, cafes and restaurants are popular evil twin spots
5.2.definition: They offer free Wi-Fi with open authentication, which makes this type of attack easy.

5.2.term: Why clients associate with the evil twin rather than the legitimate AP
5.2.definition: Those near the rogue AP find the stronger signal and most likely associate with it.
5.2.cloze: Clients near a rogue AP associate with it because it offers the ___ signal.

5.2.term: Where defeating a MITM attack begins
5.2.definition: With identifying legitimate devices on the WLAN by authenticating users; after all legitimate devices are known, the network can be monitored for abnormal devices or traffic.
5.2.ru: Сначала аутентифицировать и переписать легитимные устройства, потом искать аномальные.

5.3.definition: An early security feature where APs and some wireless routers allow the SSID beacon frame to be disabled, so wireless clients must manually configure the SSID to connect.
5.3.ru: Отключение рассылки SSID: имя сети вводится вручную.

5.3.definition: An early security feature where an administrator manually permits or denies clients wireless access based on their physical MAC hardware address.
5.3.ru: Белый или чёрный список MAC-адресов на точке доступа.

5.3.term: Why SSID cloaking and MAC filtering do not stop a crafty intruder
5.3.definition: SSIDs are easily discovered even if APs do not broadcast them, and MAC addresses can be spoofed.
5.3.ru: SSID всё равно вычисляется, а MAC подделывается.

5.3.definition: Original 802.11 authentication where any wireless client can easily connect; it should only be used where security is of no concern, such as cafes, hotels and remote areas, and the client is responsible for its own security such as a VPN.
5.3.ru: Подключается кто угодно. Только там, где безопасность не важна.

5.3.definition: Original 802.11 authentication providing mechanisms such as WEP, WPA, WPA2 and WPA3 to authenticate and encrypt data between a wireless client and AP, where the password must be pre-shared between both parties.
5.3.ru: Пароль заранее известен обеим сторонам. Сюда входят WEP, WPA, WPA2, WPA3.

5.3.definition: Wired Equivalent Privacy: the original 802.11 specification designed to secure data using the Rivest Cipher 4 (RC4) encryption method with a static key that never changes, which makes it easy to hack; it should never be used.
5.3.ru: Самый старый: RC4 со статическим ключом. Использовать нельзя.

5.3.definition: Wi-Fi Protected Access: a Wi-Fi Alliance standard that uses WEP but secures the data with the much stronger Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP), which changes the key for each packet.
5.3.ru: Поверх WEP, но с TKIP: ключ меняется на каждый пакет.

5.3.definition: The current industry standard for securing wireless networks; it uses the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for encryption.
5.3.ru: Текущий отраслевой стандарт, шифрование AES.

5.3.definition: The next generation of Wi-Fi security; all WPA3-enabled devices use the latest security methods, disallow outdated legacy protocols, and require the use of Protected Management Frames (PMF).
5.3.ru: Следующее поколение: только современные методы, обязательные PMF.

5.3.definition: WEP — оригинальная спецификация 802.11.
5.3.ru: RC4 со статическим ключом это WEP.

5.3.term: TKIP, which changes the key for each packet
5.3.definition: WPA — стандарт Wi-Fi Alliance поверх WEP.
5.3.ru: TKIP это WPA.

5.3.definition: WPA2 — текущий отраслевой стандарт.
5.3.ru: AES с CCMP это WPA2.

5.3.term: SAE and mandatory Protected Management Frames
5.3.definition: WPA3 — следующее поколение безопасности Wi-Fi.
5.3.ru: SAE и обязательные PMF это WPA3.

5.3.term: Which standard wireless networks should use until WPA3 is ubiquitous
5.3.definition: Until the availability of WPA3 devices becomes ubiquitous, wireless networks should use the WPA2 standard.
5.3.ru: Пока WPA3 не везде: использовать WPA2.

5.3.definition: Authentication mode intended for home or small office networks, where users authenticate using a pre-shared key (PSK) and no special authentication server is required.
5.3.ru: Для дома и малого офиса: общий пароль PSK, сервер не нужен.

5.3.definition: Authentication mode intended for enterprise networks that requires a RADIUS authentication server; the device is authenticated by the RADIUS server and then users authenticate using the 802.1X standard, which uses EAP.
5.3.ru: Для предприятия: нужен сервер RADIUS, пользователи по 802.1X и EAP.

5.3.definition: Pre-shared key: the shared password wireless clients use to authenticate with the wireless router in Personal mode.
5.3.ru: Общий заранее розданный пароль.

5.3.definition: Temporal Key Integrity Protocol: the encryption method used by WPA; it supports legacy WLAN equipment, encrypts the Layer 2 payload, and carries out a Message Integrity Check (MIC) in the encrypted packet.
5.3.ru: Шифрование WPA. Шифрует полезную нагрузку L2 и проверяет целостность через MIC.

5.3.definition: Advanced Encryption Standard: the encryption method used by WPA2 and the preferred, far stronger method; it uses CCMP, which allows destination hosts to recognize if the encrypted and non-encrypted bits have been altered.
5.3.ru: Шифрование WPA2, самое стойкое. Работает через CCMP.

5.3.definition: Counter Cipher Mode with Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol: the mode used by AES that allows destination hosts to recognize if the encrypted and non-encrypted bits have been altered.
aliases: counter cipher mode with block chaining message authentication code protocol
5.3.ru: Режим работы AES, замечает подмену битов.

5.3.definition: Message Integrity Check: the check TKIP carries out in the encrypted packet to ensure the message has not been altered.
5.3.ru: Проверка целостности сообщения в TKIP.

5.3.definition: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting: the server framework required by the Enterprise security mode, implemented with a RADIUS server.
5.3.ru: Аутентификация, авторизация, учёт. В Enterprise это RADIUS.

5.3.definition: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service: the AAA server that authenticates the device in WPA2-Enterprise mode.
5.3.ru: Сервер аутентификации для режима Enterprise.

5.3.term: The officially assigned RADIUS UDP ports
5.3.definition: UDP 1812 for RADIUS Authentication and UDP 1813 for RADIUS Accounting; RADIUS can also operate using UDP ports 1645 and 1646.
5.3.cloze: Officially assigned UDP ports are ___ for RADIUS Authentication and 1813 for RADIUS Accounting.
5.3.ru: 1812 аутентификация, 1813 учёт. Запасные 1645 и 1646.

5.3.definition: The standard that provides centralized, server-based authentication of end users, handling user authentication and authorization in the Enterprise mode.
5.3.ru: Централизованная серверная аутентификация пользователей.

5.3.definition: Extensible Authentication Protocol: a framework for authenticating network access, used by the 802.1X login process to communicate with the AP and RADIUS server and to negotiate a secure private key.
5.3.ru: Каркас аутентификации, по которому работает 802.1X.

5.3.term: Where the shared key must be configured
5.3.definition: Only on the AP, to authenticate it with the RADIUS server; it is not a parameter that must be configured on a wireless client.
5.3.ru: Только на точке доступа для связи с RADIUS. На клиенте не нужен.

5.3.term: The four features included in WPA3
5.3.definition: WPA3-Personal, WPA3-Enterprise, Open Networks, and Internet of Things (IoT) Onboarding.
5.3.ru: Personal, Enterprise, открытые сети, подключение IoT.

5.3.definition: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals: the WPA3-Personal feature specified in IEEE 802.11-2016 that never exposes the PSK, thwarting brute force attacks on the handshake.
5.3.ru: В WPA3-Personal: PSK не светится в эфире, брутфорс рукопожатия не работает.

5.3.definition: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption: the WPA3 feature that encrypts all wireless traffic on open or public Wi-Fi networks, which still use no authentication.
5.3.ru: Открытые сети остаются без аутентификации, но трафик шифруется.

5.3.definition: Device Provisioning Protocol: designed to onboard headless IoT devices using a hardcoded public key, typically stamped on the device as a QR code; it will replace WPS over time.
5.3.ru: Подключение IoT по QR-коду с зашитым публичным ключом. Заменяет WPS.

5.3.definition: Wi-Fi Protected Setup: the WPA2 feature to quickly onboard devices without configuring them first; it is vulnerable to a variety of attacks and is not recommended.
5.3.ru: Быстрое подключение из WPA2. Дырявое, не рекомендуется.

5.3.definition: Protected Management Frames: required by all WPA3-enabled devices.
5.3.ru: Защищённые management-кадры, обязательны в WPA3.

5.3.definition: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite: adhered to by WPA3-Enterprise, which requires a 192-bit cryptographic suite and eliminates mixing of security protocols from previous 802.11 standards.
5.3.ru: Набор алгоритмов WPA3-Enterprise, 192-битная криптография.

5.3.term: What headless means for an IoT device
5.3.definition: The device has no built-in GUI for configuration, so it needs an easy way to get connected to the wireless network.
5.3.ru: Нет экрана и интерфейса настройки.
